memos.headline: S02 and S08 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S09 and S04 Remain Broken
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. S02 is the standout: +38.2% over 12 weeks, +25.2% relative strength vs SPY over the same period, sitting just 0.6% off its 52-week high with RSI at 64.9—strong but not yet overbought. S08 is similarly positioned near its highs (drawdown only -2.1%) with a +12.2% weekly surge and solid 12w relative strength of +8.8%. S06 is essentially at a new 52-week high (drawdown -0.2%) with strong 4w relative strength of +12.4%, though its 12w relative strength is flat, which tempers my conviction slightly. On the other side, S09 is in a clear downtrend: RSI 36.7, -16.4% over 12 weeks, -29.3% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks, and 20% off its high—this is a name to avoid until it reclaims its 50-day mean. S04 is similarly weak at -28% from its 52-week high and trading 12.3% below its 200-day mean, though the +10.7% weekly bounce could be a dead-cat rally rather than a reversal.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: +38% over 12w, near 52w high, RSI 64.9 not yet extreme—would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~$390).
Clean uptrend with +21.7% 12w return, only -2.1% from highs, and positive relative strength; a break below ~$293 (50d area) would change my view.

Sitting at essentially a new 52w high with low ATR (2.46%) and strong 4w relative strength (+12.4%), but flat 12w relative strength keeps conviction moderate; watch for a close below ~$312 (50d area).
Solid 12w trend (+17.8%) and above 200d mean by 13.8%, but RSI at 49.5 and -10.6% drawdown suggest consolidation; need a reclaim above ~$370 to get constructive.
Massive 26w gain of +65.4% and +38.3% above 200d mean screams extended, and the -8.8% weekly drop with 4.63% ATR signals high volatility; trend is up but risk of mean reversion is real.
Mid-range RSI (48.7), -5% below 50d mean, and flat 12w relative strength vs SPY—no edge either way until it breaks above ~$255 or below ~$230.
Worst relative strength in the universe at -29.3% vs SPY over 12w, RSI 36.7, and -20% from highs—clear downtrend until price reclaims ~$148 (50d area).
Trading 12.3% below its 200d mean and -28% from 52w high; the +10.7% weekly bounce looks like a bear-market rally—would need a sustained close above ~$407 (50d area) to reconsider.
RSI 41.2, -7.1% below 50d mean, and -8.0% 4w relative strength vs SPY point to ongoing weakness; needs to hold ~$190 or risk accelerating lower.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Earnings Collapse Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between companies with durable, expanding margins and those facing cash-flow compression. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, a 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% YoY to $58.32B on minimal debt of $8.47B — this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin, 21.8% revenue growth, and 81.2% net income growth on just $14.79B of debt. On the other end, S09 posted a 45.8% YoY decline in net income to $4.18B on a thin 4.9% margin with $33.13B in debt, and S02 is barely growing revenue (+2.0%) with flat earnings and a 5.6% margin — neither name offers the earnings durability I require. S04 at 38.3% net margin and 23.1% net income growth with moderate leverage ($40.26B) is a solid compounder, while S06's $448.76B debt load relative to $16.49B in quarterly net income is a leverage concern despite decent margins. A sustained margin contraction at S10 or S05 would change my view on those names.

views.note: 71.5% net margin, 85% revenue growth, 211% net income growth, and only $8.47B debt — best earnings power in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 81% net income growth and minimal leverage at $14.79B debt supports durable earnings.
38.3% net margin, 18.3% revenue growth, and 23.1% net income growth with manageable $40.26B debt make this a quality compounder.
Revenue growth of 16.6% and 76.7% net income growth are encouraging, but 16.7% margin and $122.63B debt leave less room for error.
Solid 16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.70B in debt and decelerating income growth (+19.4%) keep me at neutral.
33.1% net margin is respectable but $448.76B total debt dwarfs quarterly earnings and limits upside in a rising-rate environment.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% income growth are attractive, but 14.6% margin and $36.21B debt on $17.41B revenue signal leverage risk.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin with $33.13B debt — classic cash-flow compression.
Revenue growth of just 2.0%, flat net income, 5.6% margin, and $77.92B debt offer no earnings durability.
18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are decent but unexciting; $23.85B debt on $21.23B quarterly revenue is manageable but growth is modest.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause but Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI and Flattening Curve Argue Against Duration and Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a regime that is best described as a prolonged pause with an inflationary tilt. The Fed has held the upper bound at 3.75% for at least three months, having cut 75bp over the past year, but CPI is running at +4.2% YoY (May print 333.98), which is well above target and likely freezes any further easing. The labor market is stable at 4.3% unemployment (down 10bp over three months, flat YoY), so there is no urgency to cut. Meanwhile, the 10y yield has risen 18bp over three months to 4.49% and the 10y-2y spread has compressed 21bp to just 0.31pp, signaling the market is pricing in higher-for-longer rates and possibly slower growth ahead. A CPI print that drops below 3.5% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.6% would change my regime call toward renewed easing, but until then I favor short-duration defensives and banks over growth and cyclicals.

views.note: Banks benefit from a stable-to-positive yield curve and a prolonged pause regime that keeps net interest margins healthy with the 10y at 4.49%.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the flattening curve and sticky inflation suggest late-cycle dynamics with limited upside for risk assets.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 10y yield rising 18bp to 4.49% and no near-term prospect of further Fed cuts given 4.2% CPI.
Cyclicals are vulnerable as the curve flattening (10y-2y down 21bp to 0.31pp) historically presages slowing growth, and sticky inflation limits policy support.
Energy is a mixed bag—inflation staying elevated can support commodity prices, but a growth slowdown implied by the flattening curve caps demand upside.
Without sector-specific clarity, the macro backdrop of paused rates and sticky inflation offers no strong directional signal here.

memos.headline: S09 Delisting/Acquisition Filing Signals Major Narrative Shift; S05 and S06 Show Elevated Filing Activity
memos.body: I am flagging S09 as the most significant sentiment event in the universe today: the July 1 8-K bundles a completed acquisition/disposition, a delisting notice, material rights modifications, and board changes—an unusually dense filing that typically accompanies a transformative corporate action and will dominate near-term media tone. S05 has filed six 8-Ks since May 11 including two material definitive agreements and board changes, suggesting a restructuring narrative that should keep coverage volume elevated and tone volatile. S06 has similarly high filing cadence (seven 8-Ks since May 7) with bylaws amendments, Reg FD disclosures, and a board change on June 25, but the filings are spread over routine categories and I read the tone as already digested. S10 posted a -1.8% price reaction to its May 20 earnings release, and subsequent filings have been unremarkable, so I see the negative tone as largely priced.

views.note: Delisting notice and dense transformative 8-K filed July 1 introduces extreme uncertainty and likely negative media tone shift.
High filing volume with material agreements and board turnover keeps tone volatile but direction is unclear without GDELT tone data.
Steady cadence of routine filings and a board change suggest stable but already-priced narrative with no clear tone inflection.
The -1.8% earnings reaction on May 20 was modest and subsequent filings are routine; negative tone appears priced.
New material definitive agreement and debt obligation on June 10 could shift tone positively if it signals growth investment, but conviction is low without media data.
Two board-change filings in May-June are low-signal from a sentiment perspective; no narrative shift detected.

memos.headline: Collapsing Oil and Fading Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical De-Escalation, but Flattening Curve Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see a macro backdrop where geopolitical risk premiums are unwinding rapidly: WTI crude has fallen 31.6% over three months to $69.74/bbl, and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 42% over the same period to 208.64, suggesting that sanctions/trade-war fears that dominated Q1 are receding. HY OAS at 2.74% (down 42bp over 3m) confirms credit markets are not pricing imminent supply-chain disruption or conflict escalation. However, the 10y-2y spread has narrowed 21bp over three months to just 0.31pp, and VIX ticked up 3.4% month-over-month, hinting the market senses a growth slowdown even as tail risk fades. Without specific 8-K content beyond item headers, I have limited company-level geopolitical intelligence, so my conviction is moderate; a renewed round of export controls or energy sanctions would change my view materially.

views.note: Heavy 8-K activity (five filings in two months) could reflect corporate restructuring or regulatory engagement, but without detail on sanctions or export-control exposure I stay neutral.
Three 8-K filings including Reg FD disclosure suggest active investor communication; absent evidence of direct geopolitical headwinds, I lean neutral with low conviction.
Falling oil prices and declining policy uncertainty are tailwinds for cost-sensitive industrials/consumers; single 8-K shows no red flags, and the macro de-escalation backdrop is supportive.
Recent 8-K and a benign geopolitical environment (HY OAS tightening, EPU plunging) favor risk assets; I would flip to avoid if new export controls targeting this sector emerge.
Reg FD disclosure filed in June without further context; the flattening yield curve and slight VIX uptick keep me from taking a directional view.
Single Reg FD filing in May provides minimal geopolitical signal; macro de-escalation is positive but I lack company-specific evidence to build conviction.

plan.summary: Overweight names where strong fundamentals and positive technicals converge (S05, S10), take a moderate position in the technically strongest trend (S02/S08) while sizing down where analysts conflict, and keep ~30% cash given sticky inflation, a flattening curve, and late-cycle macro signals.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst rates S05 highest conviction long (56.9% net margin, 81% NI growth); macro analyst favors it as a defensive staple in a sticky-inflation regime; technicals show solid 12w trend (+17.8%) though consolidating. Broad agreement across three analysts supports a full-sized position.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $330 (roughly 50d mean area and ~8% stop) or a quarterly margin contraction below 50% net margin.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst gives S10 the highest conviction in the universe (71.5% net margin, 85% revenue growth, 211% NI growth); geopolitics analyst is mildly supportive. However, technicals flag ongoing weakness (RSI 41.2, -7.1% below 50d mean), so I size down versus the seed and use a wider stop to respect the technical weakness.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $175 (~10% stop) which would confirm accelerating downtrend, or new export-control announcements targeting S10's sector.

plans.rationale: Technicals analyst rates S08 highly (clean uptrend, -2.1% from highs, +12.2% weekly surge); fundamentals are decent (16.6% revenue growth, 26.6% margin) though macro analyst warns of duration headwinds from rising 10y yields. Net positive but sized moderately given the macro conflict.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $290 (50d mean area, ~6% stop) or 10y yield spiking above 4.75% which would intensify duration headwinds.

plans.rationale: Technicals analyst's top pick (+38% over 12w, near 52w high, RSI 64.9), but fundamentals analyst flags 2% revenue growth, flat earnings, and 5.6% margin as unattractive. The strong technical trend earns a position but sized down due to the fundamental conflict.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $390 (50d mean) or a deterioration in relative strength vs SPY turning negative over 4 weeks.

plans.rationale: Technicals show S06 at essentially a new 52w high with low ATR (2.46%), providing a tight-stop opportunity. Fundamentals are mixed (33.1% margin but massive $449B debt), and macro/sentiment are neutral. Moderate position with a tight stop exploits the low-volatility breakout setup.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $318 (~5% stop, below 50d mean area) or rising rates pushing 10y above 4.75% pressuring the heavy debt load.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals are solid (38.3% net margin, 23.1% NI growth) and macro analyst favors banks in a pause regime with healthy NIM. However, technicals are clearly bearish (-28% from highs, below 200d mean) and the +10.7% weekly bounce may be a dead-cat rally. Tiny position as a contrarian value bet only.
plans.changes_my_mind: Failure to hold above $355 (~10% stop) or a sustained close above $407 (50d mean) would respectively confirm the downtrend or validate the reversal.
